label: Results, testimonials and “specialist” claims
text: A communication may not promise a specific result (7.2(i)). A stated result needs a description of the type of case, must be objectively verifiable, and must not mislead (7.2(m)). A testimonial must come from someone with personal, real and direct legal experience with the lawyer, and payment for it must be disclosed (7.2(l)). The rules bar judges and law-enforcement officers as endorsers unless they were clients (7.2(o)), actors playing a lawyer, or actors playing a client unless non-speaking background (7.2(p)). Dramatizations must say "Dramatization -- not (the) (an) actual event" (7.2(n)). A communication may not compare the quality of lawyers' services except as Rule 7.4 provides (7.1(c)). A lawyer may not say or imply being a specialist except as 7.4 allows (7.4).
note: Rule 7.4 contains no comparison exception; the 7.1(c) cross-reference is as the Court wrote it.

label: Referral services and lead generators
text: A lawyer must not compensate, give or promise anything of value to a person for recommending the lawyer's services (7.2(h)). Allowed: the usual costs of permitted communications; the usual charges of a not-for-profit lawyer-referral service or legal-aid agency recognized by the Office of General Counsel; sponsorship fees and charitable contributions; non-exclusive referral agreements disclosed to the client; and nominal gifts of appreciation not intended as compensation (7.2(h)(1)-(5)). A lawyer may not pay for another firm's communication unless the two have agreed to work together and jointly represent clients in that matter (7.2(h)(1)). A lawyer must not manipulate or buy search results to divert a prospective client (7.2(r)). The rules do not name lead generators.
note: Absence of a lead-generator clause is a finding from Rule 7.2 as read. No Alabama State Bar opinion on lead generators was found.

label: Privacy and health-data law
text: The Alabama Personal Data Protection Act (HB 351, Act 2026-552, approved April 16, 2026) takes effect May 1, 2027. It applies to persons that do business in Alabama or target Alabama residents and control or process the data of more than 25,000 consumers (payment-only data excluded), or derive more than 25 percent of gross revenue from selling personal data. A business with fewer than 500 employees is exempt if it does not sell personal data.

label: Results, testimonials and “specialist” claims
text: An ad may not contain a guarantee or warranty of success, a claim of immediate cash or quick settlement, an impersonation, an undisclosed dramatization, a spokesperson without a disclosed title, misleading statements about skills, experience or record, or an award that comes with membership or a fee (B&P 6157.2(a)). Rule 7.1 comment [4] says a testimonial or endorsement can mislead if it creates an unjustified expectation of the same results. In electronic media (television, radio or computer networks), a message about a case result shown out of context, displays of injuries or accident scenes, and references to money received or potential recovery are presumed false or misleading (6158.1); portrayed results need either the facts or a statement that results depend on the facts of that case (6158.3). A lawyer may say "certified specialist" only if certified by the Board of Legal Specialization or another State Bar-accredited entity, with the certifier named (Rule 7.4(a)). A consumer misled by an ad may sue after a State Bar finding for $5,000 to $100,000 per unique ad or three times actual damages (6157.2(c)).
note: The rules have no separate testimonial ban; Rule 7.1 and B&P 6157.1-6158.3 apply.

label: Referral services and lead generators
text: A lawyer may not compensate, promise or give anything of value to a person to recommend or secure the lawyer's services, except to pay reasonable ad costs, the usual charges of a legal services plan or a qualified lawyer referral service (one run under the State Bar's minimum standards), a practice sale, non-exclusive reciprocal referral arrangements the client is told about, and a gift after a recommendation led to hiring if not promised in advance (Rule 7.2(b)). Employees, agents and vendors providing marketing services may be paid (7.2 comment [3]). A lawyer referral service must be State Bar certified (B&P 6155(a)(1)), and anyone may sue over an uncertified service for $5,000 to $100,000 per violation or three times actual damages (6156.5). A San Diego County Bar Association ethics opinion (2019-2) found that a for-profit program that collects a flat fee and keeps a marketing fee of about 20 to 30 percent is fee-sharing and not a certified service.

label: Results, testimonials and “specialist” claims
text: References to past results must be objectively verifiable, and a prediction or guaranty of results is deceptive (Rule 4-7.13(b)(1)-(2)). Comparisons and words that characterize a lawyer's skills, experience, reputation or record must be objectively verifiable (4-7.13(b)(3)). A testimonial must be the person's actual experience, represent what clients generally experience, not be written by the lawyer, not be paid for, and carry a disclaimer that the client may not obtain the same or similar results (4-7.13(b)(9)). "Board certified" requires certification by the Florida Bar plan or an ABA- or Bar-accredited program, with the area and certifier named (4-7.14(a)(4)). "Specialist" or "expert" requires such certification or objectively verifiable education, training, experience or substantial involvement (4-7.14(a)(5)). A celebrity's voice or image is barred unless a current or former client's testimonial or a local announcer who gives no endorsement (4-7.15(c)).

label: Results, testimonials and “specialist” claims
text: A communication may not be false, deceptive or misleading (7.10). AAC Regulation 1 says ads may be misleading if they create an unjustified expectation, compare lawyers without factual proof, or show an actor posing as an actual client. General testimonials about satisfaction are ordinarily not misleading. Damage awards, cumulative verdicts or a verdict record need the case's facts and law. A lawyer may say they are certified as a specialist only if the body is state-approved or ABA-accredited, is named, and the certification is current (7.40(4)).

label: Referral services and lead generators
text: A lawyer may not compensate or give anything of value to a person or organization to recommend or obtain employment by a client (7.2(a)). Exceptions: a contract with a nonlegal professional firm under Rule 5.8, and usual fees of a qualified legal assistance organization or referral fees to another lawyer under Rule 1.5(g). NYSBA ethics opinions: 1294 (March 12, 2026) allows pay-per-lead from a platform that does not recommend the lawyer, uses neutral disclosed criteria and does not vary the price with a hire or the fee. 1279 (February 20, 2025) bars flat "administrative" payments to referrers. 1267 (June 18, 2024) finds a payment to a site that promises vetted lawyers is an improper payment for a recommendation. 1271 (August 22, 2024) finds a percentage-of-fee payment to a bidding platform breaks the rule on sharing fees with non-lawyers (5.4(a)).
note: The ethics opinions are the New York State Bar Association's, a voluntary bar; they are not court rulings.

label: Results, testimonials and “specialist” claims
text: A communication may not be false or misleading, or omit a fact needed to keep it from misleading (7.1). Results may mislead if they create an unjustified expectation of the same outcome, and an unsubstantiated comparison may mislead (7.1 cmt. [3]). West Virginia does not recognize specialization, so a lawyer may not state or imply being certified as a specialist (7.4(d)). Firm names may not violate 7.1 (7.5(a)). The rules have no testimonial clause.

label: Referral services and lead generators
text: A lawyer may not give anything of value for recommending the lawyer's services, except ad costs, the usual charges of a legal service plan or a not-for-profit or qualified lawyer referral service, a practice sale, and non-exclusive reciprocal referrals with client notice (7.2(b)). A lawyer may pay for client leads if the generator does not recommend the lawyer, imply a recommendation or hide that the lawyer paid (7.2 cmt. [5]). The Lawyer Disciplinary Board's L.E.O. 2018-01 (entered June 27, 2018) says a per-case "marketing fee" paid to a for-profit matching service is an impermissible referral fee and endorsement fee.
